title: Computing within a space bound
statement: A finite Turing machine $M$ computes a function $f$ within space bound $s$ if, for every Boolean string $x$, there is a time $t$ at which $M$ outputs $f(x)$ and uses at most $s(|x|)$ space, measured from its initial configuration on $x$.
hypotheses_covered: A finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
A function from Boolean strings to Boolean strings
A space bound from natural input lengths to natural numbers
For every Boolean input string, some time exists at which the machine computes the output and satisfies the space bound
